cord an eval start](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/authenticate-and-record-an-eval-start.md): Called by official
SDK, CLI and Vitest runners before executing an eval. Requires an organization API key or saved-login bearer. Records only start m
etadata, creates no dashboard run, and applies no debit or quota draw. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage. Reuse t
he runStartId for ret…\n124:- [Open a run for incremental ingestion](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/open-a-run-fo
r-incremental-ingestion.md): Opens a run that iterations are appended to, for a long CI job that reports as it goes. Pair with `ru
ns/iterations` and `runs/finalize`.\n125:- [Get a run's gate waiver](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/get-a-runs-ga
te-waiver.md): The waiver in force over this run, or `null`. Available to anyone who can VIEW the run, not only to those who can g
rant one: a waiver its readers cannot see is not a visible waiver.\n126:- [Waive a run gate](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference
/eval-runs/waive-a-run-gate.md): Override a FAILING run's release gate until an expiry you name. This does NOT make the run pass:
the run keeps its `result`, the waiver is a separate audited record, and every surface that honors it, such as the CLI's `eval gat
e`, reports the gate as waived, by whom, why, and until when.\n127:- [Revoke a gate waiver](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/
eval-runs/revoke-a-gate-waiver.md): End a waiver early, putting the gate back. Requires the manage tier.\n128:- [Preview determini
stic draft evaluators against stored evidence](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/preview-deterministic-draft-evaluat
ors-against-stored-evidence.md): Requires suite configuration permission and a terminal run. Reserves a 60-second deterministic-pr
eview cooldown, independent of judge previews. Supply the returned continuation object with the unchanged draft to read the next b
ounded population. Reads at most 100 iterations within a 30-second operat…\n130:- [Get the authenticated account](https://docs.mcp
jam.com/api-reference/catalog/get-the-authenticated-account.md): The user behind the API key (keys act as their creator, scoped to
one organization).\n131:- [Read the organization's spend budget](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/read-the-organizat
ions-spend-budget.md): The ceiling on what this organization may spend on MCPJam-billed work (chat, evals, judges and computer tim
e) in the current billing window, and how much of it has been spent.\n134:- [List organizations](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-refer
ence/catalog/list-organizations.md): The organizations the caller belongs to: the source of the `organizationId` that `GET /projec
ts` filters by and `POST /projects` accepts. An API key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one. Read-only: organ
ization, member, role and billing changes are not part of the public API.\n137:- [List a project's eval suites](https://docs.mcpja
m.com/api-reference/catalog/list-a-projects-eval-suites.md): Eval suites in the project with latest-run summaries and pass-rate tr
ends: the `suiteId`s the eval-run routes take.\n144:- [Delete a client](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/clients/delete-a-cli
ent.md): Permanently deletes the client. Refused while a live environment, an active legacy goal or an eval suite still holds it:
the error names what to detach first. Guest callers are denied (a write).\n167:- [List a suite's settings history](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/list-a-suites-settings-history.md): One entry per committed edit to the suite's settings, newes
t first: who made it, which STORED fields moved, the note they left, how many runs were launched against it, and the revision grou
p that ties one request's writes together. Rows carry no configuration snapshots. Send a `revisionNumber` back…\n168:- [Attach one
environment to a suite (atomic append)](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/attach-one-environment-to-a-suite-atomi
c-append.md): APPEND one project environment to the suite's attachments, if it is not already there.\n169:- [List a server's accou
nts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/list-a-servers-accounts.md): The accounts this server signs in with tha
t you can see: your own personal accounts, or, on a server shared with the project, its project accounts. Another member's persona
l account never appears. METADATA ONLY: no account response carries a token.\n170:- [Get a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com
/api-reference/server-accounts/get-a-server-account.md): One account, by id or name. Another member's personal account answers `40
4`, the same as a missing one. A name two accounts share answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_ambiguous\"` and both id
s in `details.accountIds`.\n171:- [Upload tokens to a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/upload
-tokens-to-a-server-account.md): Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id). A well-formed accoun
t id never creates one: an unknown id is `404`. Any other reference is a name, and a name no account has creates the account.\n172
:- [Delete a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/delete-a-server-account.md): Deletes the accoun
t and its stored token. The token's issuer is asked to revoke it where the issuer supports revocation (best effort), which also in
validates any copy of the same token you hold.\n173:- [Rename a server account or make it the default](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api
-reference/server-accounts/rename-a-server-account-or-make-it-the-default.md): Rename the account, make it the default, or both; a
rename applies first. A name another account on the server uses answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_taken\"`.\n174:-
[Import OAuth tokens](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/oauth/import-oauth-tokens.md): **Deprecated.** Use `PUT /projects/{pr
ojectId}/servers/{serverId}/accounts/{account}`. This route uploads to your default account on the server, creating an unnamed one
when the server has none, and is removed 90 days after the accounts API shipped. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a `Sun
se…\n179:- [Save a server into a project](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/servers/save-a-server-into-a-project.md): Creates
a saved MCP server and responds `201` with its detail. This is the provisioning entry point: every eval, host and environment rout
e addresses servers that were created here. Names are unique per workspace, so a clash responds `409` rather than silently returni
ng the existing row. Secret-bear…\n180:- [List a server's revisions](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/servers/list-a-servers-
revisions.md): A saved server's stored revisions, newest first. A revision is a capture of the server's tools and server info, rec
orded whenever they change on a connect, an eval run or a chat session. Reads stored data and never connects to the server, so it
works for stdio servers too. A server the caller cannot…\n207:- [Usage breakdown](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/us
age-breakdown.md): Which models, tools and servers the study's sessions used.\n211:- [Request insights for the current window](htt
ps://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/studies/request-insights-for-the-current-window.md): **No credits are consumed**: the model cos
t is on MCPJam. Runs a model over the study's current window and draws on the organization's `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts
REQUESTS and is SHARED with eval-run and swarm run insights, so a request here takes one from there.\n215:- [Create (or revive) a
relay tunnel for a named project server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/tunnels/create-or-revive-a-relay-tunnel-for-a-name
